        "notes": "The whole programme as one grid: a table per day, rooms across the top, the start time down the side, and each cell giving the session’s language, title, presenter and difficulty.         "id": "ddd10-about",

        "via": {
          "provider": "wayback",
          "timestamp": "20100512191629",
          "captureUrl": "https://web.archive.org/web/20100512191629/http://www.drupal-dev-days.de/de/about"
        },
        "notes": "The organisers describe this as \"das erste deutschsprachige DrupalCamp\" — the first German-language DrupalCamp — for developers and theme developers, aimed at strengthening the Drupal network across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with room for around 350 people. That is worth stating plainly next to two later claims in this series: Brussels 2011 called itself \"the first European Drupal Developer Days conference\", and Barcelona 2012 called itself the second edition, \"the first one took place in Brussels\". Munich predates both and ran under the Developer Days name, but as a German-speaking regional event; the later editions were counting the pan-European series. All three statements are true as written."

      "full_description": "I had proposed this session for DrupalCon SF:\n\nI have come across a fair amount of code in my day, and I don't claim perfection for myself, but so often I see code that literally hurts my eyes and makes my brain just go numb. And in case you were not aware, bad code kills badgers (why does it have to be kittens all the time?).\n\nSo, I am here to save the badgers. I, Alan Palazzolo, the Morbus-wanna-be, am going to tell it to you straight: coding standards will get you a hot date (gender indifferent). That's no lie. All you have to do is manage a ticket to DrupalCon San Francisco (and vote for this session), and you will learn how to code wtih Drupal standards, get a date from anyone, and most importantly, save those cuddly badgers.\n\nThe most important thing to remember when writing code is to think: What will I think of this in two year's time? Someone else is probably going to read your code, even if it is not a contributed module. And you could save that person lots of time by just learning some standards and sticking to them. Now think what if YOU were that other person? Yeah, exactly, YOU are that other coder (or will be soon). Isn't that enough to care?\n\nBut wait, there's more! Coding standards allows us, as a Drupal, open-source, community solve problems more effectively. Agreeing on standards helps break down communication barriers and facilitates elegant code. Not to mention, standards really keep the stupid flame wars about dot operators down to a minimum. We all come to Drupal with our previous notions of coding habits, but accepting Drupal coding standards allows us to focus on the important things (not the space before or after the dot operator).\n\nMy talk will be about the current Drupal coding standards and how you can follow them. I will also go into where standards are going and where we could use some help in creating more and better standards, in my opinion. So act now! I promise lots of badly-photoshoped pictures of badgers.\n\n**Language:** English  \n**Session type:** Vortrag (45 Minuten)  \n**Difficulty:** Anfänger",

      "full_description": "Drupal 7 introduced the notion of **Fields**, small pieces of data you can add to several kind of **Entities**. In this session we will show how Fields are changing the way we write modules, for the better.\n\nNote: this is an (revised and improved) version of the [session I gave at Drupalcon San Francisco](http://sf2010.drupal.org/conference/sessions/how-drupal-7-fields-are-changing-way-you-write-modules).\n\n**From columns to fields**\n\nIn the beginning, there was tables and columns. Now here are fields, a dynamic way to build data models.\n\n**From nodes, users and comments to entities**\n\nIn the beginning, there was separate realms. The concept of entity unify those realms and bring them to a whole new dimension.\n\n**Case study: A Case Tracker in 100 lines**\n\nSpanning across entities, fields can be used to easily build powerful data models. Here we will see how to rewrite, from the ground up, the Case Tracker module in less then 100 lines.\n\n**Guidelines for using fields and entities efficiently in your modules**\n\nWe will describe how to use fields and entities efficiently in your module, and take the example of Drupal Commerce module as a case study.\n\n**Language:** English  \n**Session type:** Vortrag (45 Minuten)  \n**Difficulty:** Fortgeschritten",

      "startTime": "2010-05-09T13:00:00.000Z",
      "endTime": "2010-05-09T14:00:00.000Z",
      "duration": "P60M",
      "title": "Git - mal ganz einfach und praktisch!",
      "location": "Microsoft",
      "track": [],
      "speakers": [
        "EugenMayer"
      ],
      "full_description": "Auf dem Drupal-Camp in Essen beim selbigen Vortrag ist mir aufgefallen, welch verschobene Meinungen es von Git gibt.\n\nDie typischen Dinge wie:\n\n- Es sei zu kompliziert zu benutzen.\n\n- Es hat keinen wirklichen Mehrwert verglichen zu SVN/CVS\n\n- Man müsste viel neues lernen\n\n- Es sei \"nur dezentral\" und kann nicht zentral Benutzt werden\n\n- Es gibt keine grafischen Tools\n\n- Es gibt keine Integrationen in IDEs wie Eclipse, Komodo etc.\n\nIch möchte nicht nur mit diesen Vorurteilen aufräumen sondern erklären, wie man Git benutztz. Hierbei werde ich ganz am Anfang starten, ihr braucht also keine Vorkenntnisse.\n\nZiel:\n\nIhr geht aus dieser Session raus und habt das Gefühl, dass ihr Git beherrscht (und nicht anders herum). Ihr sollt direkt Anfangen können, Git produktiv einsetzen zu können und damit sozusagen \"morgen CVS oder SVN\" zu ersetzen. Ihr werde wissen, was \"mit Git arbeiten\" bedeutet und was eigentlich der wahre nutzen von Dingen wie \"Short Topic Branch, Long Topic branch, Merge, Branch, Remotes\" ist.\n\nKein Ziel ist:\n\nEin religiöse Diskussion ob Git, Bzr, Mercurial oder andere neuzeitliche SCM-Systeme. Ich denke, egal welches Ihr von diesen SCM nehmt, ihr habt so oder so enorm einen enormen Vorteil gegenüber CVS und SVN. Nehmt als bitte einfach eines von diesen - mir ist nicht wichtig welches.\n\n**Language:** Deutsch  \n**Difficulty:** Anfänger",

      "track": [],

      ],
      "full_description": "Es gibt viele Wege, um Daten zwischen Drupal-Websites auszutauschen. Von einfachen Multisite-Installationen mit gemeinsam genutzten Node-Tabellen bis hin zur automatisierten Synchronisierung über RSS-Feeds oder Webservices. Auch unterschiedliche Modelle des Austauschs wie zentrale Websites, die Inhalte an Affiliates senden oder Netzwerke von Sites, die Daten untereinander austauschen, sind möglich.\n\nDiese Session versucht einen Überblick über die verschiedenen Methoden zu geben, beleuchtet die dafür jeweils notwendigen Module und Konfigurationen und zeigt Best Practices auf. Vor- und Nachteile der jeweiligen Ansätze werden diskutiert.\n\nJe nach Teilnehmerwunsch kann auch auf den Datenimport von externen Quellen wie Flickr, RSS-Feeds oder Youtube eingegangen werden.\n\n**Language:** Deutsch  \n**Session type:** Vortrag (45 Minuten)  \n**Difficulty:** Anfänger",
